Assertion (A): The Head of School is required to conduct periodic random inspections and physical verifications of store items and stock registers.
Reason (R): Regular physical verification deters misappropriation, detects pilferage, and ensures that actual on-ground inventory aligns with book records.
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation_english:
Under General Financial Rules (GFR), 2017 (Rules 213 to 215) and the financial control guidelines of the Directorate of Education, Delhi:

1. Custody and Accounting of Stores: The Head of Office (HOO) / Head of School (HoS) is responsible for the proper custody, maintenance, and periodic physical verification of all fixed assets, consumable stores, laboratory apparatus, sports equipment, and library books.
2. Surprise & Periodic Checks: In addition to the mandatory annual physical verification, the HoS is required to conduct surprise and random checks of the stock ledger against the physical inventory to ensure operational integrity (Assertion A is true).
3. Purpose of Verification: Physical verification directly safeguards public assets by preventing pilferage, identifying missing or damaged items, unearthing discrepancies between recorded balances and shelf stock, and initiating timely condemnation procedures (Reason R is true).

Since the Reason provides the exact administrative and financial rationale for why Assertion A is mandated, Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation_hindi:
सामान्य वित्तीय नियम (GFR), 2017 (नियम 213 से 215) और दिल्ली शिक्षा निदेशालय के वित्तीय प्रशासन संबंधी दिशा-निर्देशों के अनुसार:

1. स्टॉक का रखरखाव: कार्यालय प्रमुख (HOO) / स्कूल प्रमुख (HoS) स्कूल की सभी अचल संपत्तियों, उपभोज्य सामग्री (consumables), विज्ञान प्रयोगशाला उपकरण, खेल सामग्री और पुस्तकालय पुस्तकों के उचित रखरखाव और भौतिक सत्यापन के लिए जिम्मेदार होता है।
2. औचक निरीक्षण: वार्षिक भौतिक सत्यापन के अतिरिक्त, स्कूल प्रमुख को वर्ष भर में औचक और यादृच्छिक रूप से स्टॉक रजिस्टरों और वास्तविक भंडार की जांच करनी होती है (अभिकथन A सही है)।
3. कारण और औचित्य: इस भौतिक सत्यापन का मुख्य उद्देश्य सामग्री की चोरी, गबन, दुरुपयोग को रोकना तथा यह सुनिश्चित करना है कि रजिस्टर में दर्ज संख्या और मौके पर मौजूद भौतिक वस्तुएं एक-दूसरे से मेल खाती हैं (कारण R सही है)।

चूंकि कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सटीक तार्किक और वैधानिक व्याख्या प्रस्तुत करता है, अतः विकल्प A सही उत्तर है।

questions.question_english: The 'SMC Fund' allocated to government schools in Delhi is primarily intended for which of the following?
options_english: Minor repairs and localized school needs approved by SMC
Organizing international professional study visits and foreign exposure tours for teaching staff
Disbursing performance-linked annual financial bonuses directly to the Head of School
Fully subsidizing daily commute and private bus transport costs for all enrolled students
questions.explanation_english:
Under **Section 21 of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009**, read with guidelines issued by the Directorate of Education (DoE), Delhi:

1. **Decentralized Governance**: To empower the local community, parents, and school staff in the day-to-day upkeep of schools, the DoE provides untied funds directly under the purview of the **School Management Committee (SMC)**.
2. **Permissible Usage**: The SMC Fund must be utilized based on formal resolutions passed by the SMC for localized requirements, including:
   - Minor civil and electrical repairs (e.g., fixing broken window panes, locks, doors, benches, switches, and fans).
   - Urgent plumbing and sanitation fixes for drinking water points and toilets.
   - Procurement of emergency teaching aids, stationery, and learning materials.
   - Community mobilization events, parent engagement workshops, and local child safety initiatives.
3. **Prohibited Expenditures**: It cannot be diverted for international tours, personal bonuses or honorariums for the Head of School, or providing private school bus transportation.
questions.explanation_hindi:
निःशुल्क और अनिवार्य बाल शिक्षा का अधिकार (RTE) अधिनियम, 2009 की **धारा 21** तथा शिक्षा निदेशालय (DoE), दिल्ली सरकार के दिशा-निर्देशों के अनुसार:

1. **विकेंद्रीकृत स्कूल प्रबंधन:** स्कूलों के स्थानीय स्तर पर प्रबंधन में अभिभावकों और समुदाय की भागीदारी सुनिश्चित करने के लिए **स्कूल प्रबंधन समिति निधि (SMC Fund)** प्रदान की जाती है।
2. **अनुमन्य कार्य:** इस निधि का उपयोग SMC की बैठक में पारित प्रस्ताव के आधार पर स्कूल की तात्कालिक आवश्यकताओं के लिए किया जाता है:
   - स्कूल परिसर की छोटी मरम्मत (जैसे टूटी खिड़कियां, दरवाजे, डेस्क-बेंच, ताले, पंखे और बिजली के उपकरण ठीक कराना)।

   - तात्कालिक शिक्षण-अधिगम सामग्री, स्टेशनरी और सामुदायिक जागरूकता कार्यक्रमों का आयोजन।
3. **प्रतिबंधित व्यय:** इस निधि का उपयोग स्टाफ की विदेश यात्राओं, स्कूल प्रमुख को व्यक्तिगत वित्तीय बोनस देने अथवा निजी बस परिवहन सेवाओं पर खर्च करने के लिए कतई नहीं किया जा सकता।

questions.explanation_english: Under Rule 43-C of the Central Civil Services (Leave) Rules, 1972, Child Care Leave (CCL) is admissible to female Government servants (and single male Government servants) for a maximum period of 730 days during their entire service career. CCL is granted for taking care of up to two eldest surviving children (below 18 years of age, or of any age in the case of a disabled child) for rearing or addressing needs like examinations or medical care. In terms of remuneration, 100% of leave salary is paid for the first 365 days, and 80% is paid for the subsequent 365 days. The leave cannot be granted in more than 3 spells in a calendar year and generally for not less than 5 days per spell.
questions.explanation_hindi: CCS (अवकाश) नियम, 1972 के नियम 43-C के अनुसार, महिला सरकारी कर्मचारियों (तथा एकल पुरुष सरकारी कर्मचारियों) को अपने संपूर्ण सेवाकाल के दौरान अधिकतम 730 दिन (2 वर्ष) का बाल देखभाल अवकाश (Child Care Leave - CCL) दिया जा सकता है। यह अवकाश दो सबसे बड़े जीवित बच्चों (18 वर्ष की आयु तक, अथवा दिव्यांग बच्चों के मामले में किसी भी आयु तक) के पालन-पोषण, बीमारी अथवा परीक्षा संबंधी आवश्यकताओं की देखभाल के लिए अनुमन्य है। वेतन के संदर्भ में, प्रथम 365 दिनों के लिए 100% अवकाश वेतन और अगले 365 दिनों के लिए 80% अवकाश वेतन देय होता है। यह अवकाश एक कैलेंडर वर्ष में 3 बार (Spells) से अधिक नहीं लिया जा सकता।

questions.question_english: In the administrative context of government service, pay scales, and allowances, what does the acronym 'MACP' stand for?
options_english: Mandatory Annual Confidential Performance
Minimum Allowance for Contractual Personnel
Maximum Admissible Compensatory Pay
Modified Assured Career Progression
questions.explanation_english:
MACP stands for 'Modified Assured Career Progression' Scheme.

Key features and administrative provisions of MACP:
1. Origin & Implementation: The MACP Scheme was introduced by the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) via OM dated 19th May 2009 pursuant to the recommendations of the 6th Central Pay Commission (CPC) and continued under the 7th CPC.
2. Stagnation Relief: It is designed to alleviate stagnation and frustration among government employees (including teachers and school administrative staff) who do not receive regular promotions due to the absence of promotional hierarchy vacancies.
3. Benchmark Intervals: Financial upgradations under MACP are granted upon completion of 10, 20, and 30 years of continuous regular service in the same post/grade, or 10 years from the date of the last promotion/upgradation, whichever is earlier.
4. Nature of Benefit: It grants purely financial placement into the next immediate higher Level in the Pay Matrix without involving functional elevation, designation change, or assumption of higher duties.
5. Screening & APAR: Grants are subject to clearance by a Departmental Screening Committee (DSC) evaluating the prescribed benchmark in Annual Performance Assessment Reports (APAR) and vigilance clearance.
questions.explanation_hindi:
सरकारी सेवा, वेतन संरचना और भत्तों के संदर्भ में MACP का पूर्ण रूप 'Modified Assured Career Progression' (संशोधित सुनिश्चित करियर प्रगति) है।

योजना के प्रमुख प्रशासनिक पहलू:
1. प्रारंभ: छठे केंद्रीय वेतन आयोग (6th CPC) की सिफारिशों के आधार पर कार्मिक एवं प्रशिक्षण विभाग (DoPT) द्वारा मई 2009 में इसे लागू किया गया था और 7वें वेतन आयोग में भी यह निरंतर है।
2. उद्देश्य: संवर्ग में नियमित पदोन्नति के अवसरों के अभाव के कारण उत्पन्न होने वाली वेतन शिथिलता (stagnation) को दूर करना।
3. सेवा अंतराल: नियमित सेवा के 10, 20 और 30 वर्ष पूरे होने पर, या पिछले वित्तीय उन्नयन/पदोन्नति से 10 वर्ष व्यतीत होने पर तीन वित्तीय उन्नयन प्रदान किए जाते हैं।
4. लाभ का स्वरूप: यह केवल वित्तीय उन्नयन (Pay Matrix के अगले उच्च लेवल में स्थान) है, जिससे कर्मचारी का पदनाम या कार्यात्मक दायित्व नहीं बदलता।
5. शर्तें: यह विभागीय स्क्रीनिंग कमेटी (DSC) द्वारा वार्षिक कार्य निष्पादन मूल्यांकन रिपोर्ट (APAR) और सतर्कता अनापत्ति (Vigilance Clearance) के सत्यापन के अधीन प्रदान किया जाता है।

Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Under Section 10(1) of the Delhi School Education Act, 1973, the scales of pay and allowances of employees of a recognized private school shall not be less than those of the employees of the corresponding status in schools run by the appropriate authority.
Reason (R): Private schools receive absolute autonomy in financial matters under Article 30 of the Constitution, irrespective of state regulations.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct option:
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation_english: Assertion (A) is correct: Section 10(1) of the Delhi School Education Act (DSEA), 1973, explicitly provides that the scales of pay and allowances, medical facilities, pension, gratuity, and provident fund of employees of a recognized private school shall not be less than those of employees of corresponding status in schools run by the appropriate authority (government/local bodies). Reason (R) is incorrect: While Article 30 of the Constitution protects the fundamental right of religious and linguistic minorities to establish and administer educational institutions, this right is not absolute and does not grant immunity from state welfare regulations. questions.explanation_english:
Rule 18(2) of the Central Civil Services (Conduct) Rules, 1964 provides explicit guidelines regarding immovable property transactions:
1. No Government servant shall, except with the previous knowledge of the prescribed authority, acquire or dispose of any immovable property by lease, mortgage, purchase, sale, gift or otherwise either in his own name or in the name of any member of his family.
2. The rule further provides that if such a transaction is conducted with a person having official dealings with the Government servant, or otherwise than through a regular or reputed dealer, prior sanction of the prescribed authority is mandatory.
3. Where the transaction is through a regular or reputed dealer, giving 'previous knowledge' (prior intimation in prescribed Form I) to the competent administrative authority suffices.
4. Merely reporting the transaction ex-post in the Annual Immovable Property Return (IPR) does not fulfill the statutory requirement of Rule 18(2).
Therefore, option (a) is correct.

questions.explanation_english: Rule 11 of the CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965 divides disciplinary penalties into two categories: Minor Penalties (clauses i to iv) and Major Penalties (clauses v to ix). Minor Penalties include: (i) Censure (formal administrative reprimand recorded in service book/APAR); (ii) Withholding of promotion; (iii) Recovery from pay of the whole or part of any pecuniary loss caused to the Government by negligence or breach of orders; (iii-a) Reduction to a lower stage in the time-scale of pay by one stage for a period not exceeding 3 years, without cumulative effect and not adversely affecting pension; and (iv) Withholding of increments of pay without cumulative effect. On the other hand, Major Penalties include: reduction to a lower stage with cumulative effect or affecting pension, reduction to a lower time-scale/grade/post, compulsory retirement, removal from service, and dismissal from service. Therefore, 'Censure' is a minor penalty, whereas reduction in rank, compulsory retirement, and removal are major penalties requiring detailed inquiry under Rule 14.
questions.explanation_hindi: CCS (CCA) नियमावली, 1965 का नियम 11 शास्तियों को दो भागों में विभाजित करता है: लघु शास्तियां (Minor Penalties) और दीर्घ शास्तियां (Major Penalties)। लघु शास्तियों (खंड i से iv) में शामिल हैं: (i) परिनिंदा (Censure) - औपचारिक प्रशासनिक चेतावनी जो सेवा पंजिका में दर्ज होती है; (ii) पदोन्नति को रोकना; (iii) लापरवाही अथवा आदेशों के उल्लंघन के कारण सरकार को हुई किसी वित्तीय हानि की वेतन से वसूली; (iii-क) बिना संचयी प्रभाव के अधिकतम 3 वर्ष की अवधि के लिए वेतन में एक प्रक्रम की कमी; तथा (iv) बिना संचयी प्रभाव के वेतन वृद्धि (इंक्रीमेंट) रोकना। इसके विपरीत, अनिवार्य सेवानिवृत्ति (Compulsory Retirement), सेवा से हटाया जाना (Removal), सेवा से बर्खास्तगी (Dismissal), तथा निचले वेतनमान या पद पर अवनति दीर्घ शास्तियां (Major Penalties) हैं, जिनके लिए नियम 14 के तहत औपचारिक जांच आवश्यक होती है। अतः 'परिनिंदा' (Censure) लघु शास्ति है।

questions.explanation_english:
Both statements Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the direct and correct legal explanation of Assertion (A):

1. Section 4 of the RTE Act, 2009 Mandate: Section 4 provides that where a child above six years of age has not been admitted in any school or having been admitted, could not complete his or her elementary education, then he or she shall be admitted in a class appropriate to his or her age ('age-appropriate admission').
2. Implementation by Directorate of Education (DoE): To enforce Section 4 systematically and maintain age-homogeneity across classrooms, DoE Delhi annually issues an official Admission Circular prescribing strict minimum and maximum age criteria for classes from Pre-School/Nursery up to Class IX and XI.
3. Bridging Support via Special Training: For children who are over-age and have missed formal schooling, the law prescribes Special Training Centres (STCs) to provide accelerated bridge education so that they can seamlessly integrate into regular age-appropriate classes.
4. Causal Relationship: Because the RTE Act mandates that admission must be age-appropriate rather than arbitrary, educational administrations are obligated to formulate well-defined age boundaries for each class. Therefore, R accurately explains A.

2. शिक्षा निदेशालय (DoE) की प्रवेश नीति: धारा 4 के वैधानिक क्रियान्वयन और कक्षा में सहपाठी शिक्षण (peer learning) का संतुलन बनाए रखने हेतु शिक्षा निदेशालय प्रतिवर्ष प्रवेश परिपत्र जारी करता है, जिसमें नर्सरी/केजी से लेकर कक्षा 9वीं और 11वीं तक न्यूनतम एवं अधिकतम आयु सीमा तय की जाती है।

4. कारण और प्रभाव का संबंध: चूंकि आरटीई अधिनियम आयु-अनुरूप प्रवेश को अनिवार्य बनाता है, इसी कारण स्कूलों में कक्षाओं के लिए आयु सीमा का निर्धारण किया जाता है। अतः R, A की सही व्याख्या है।

questions.explanation_english:
Under Section 5 and Rule 46 of the Delhi School Education Act and Rules (DSEAR), 1973, no managing committee of any recognized private school (aided or unaided) is permitted to close down the school or any existing class/section without obtaining the prior formal approval of the Director of Education, GNCTD.

Key Provisions & Administrative Significance:
1. Statutory Notice & Approval (Rule 46): The managing committee must submit a formal application giving adequate written notice stating the valid educational, administrative, or financial grounds for proposed closure. Discontinuation of classes cannot be done arbitrarily or abruptly.
2. Protection of Students' Educational Rights: This mandatory requirement prevents unilateral school closures that could jeopardize students' academic continuum, disrupt their board examination preparations, and violate their right to education under the RTE Act, 2009.
3. Safeguarding Employees' Tenure: Unilateral closure could lead to unlawful termination of teachers and non-teaching staff. Requiring the Director's sanction ensures that statutory retrenchment or absorption procedures (under Section 8) are strictly monitored.
4. Regulatory Oversight: Even though the SMC or Managing Committee manages day-to-day governance, the regulatory jurisdiction over recognition, affiliation, and closure rests solely with the Directorate of Education.
questions.explanation_hindi:
दिल्ली स्कूल शिक्षा अधिनियम और नियम (DSEAR), 1973 की धारा 5 तथा नियम 46 (Rule 46) के तहत, किसी भी मान्यता प्राप्त निजी स्कूल (सहायता प्राप्त या गैर-सहायता प्राप्त) की प्रबंध समिति शिक्षा निदेशक (Director of Education), दिल्ली सरकार की पूर्व औपचारिक अनुमति के बिना स्कूल या उसकी किसी मौजूदा कक्षा/वर्ग को बंद नहीं कर सकती है।

प्रमुख प्रशासनिक बिंदु एवं वैधानिक प्रावधान:

questions.explanation_english: Section 4(1)(b) of the Right to Information Act, 2005 mandates proactive or 'Suo Moto' disclosure by all public authorities, including government schools. Under this statutory provision, every school must publish and periodically update seventeen (17) specific manuals/categories of information in the public domain (via school notice boards and the official portal). This includes the organization's particulars, powers and duties of officers and employees, decision-making procedures, rules and regulations, directory of officers/teachers, monthly remuneration, budget allocations and expenditures, subsidy/welfare schemes (such as uniforms, textbooks, scholarships, PM POSHAN), and details of Public Information Officers (PIO / APIO). The objective is to make maximum information freely accessible to parents and citizens so that they need not resort to filing formal RTI applications.

questions.explanation_english:
The National Pension System (NPS) was introduced by the Government of India via Ministry of Finance Notification No. 5/7/2003-ECB & PR dated 22nd December 2003:

1. Effective Cut-off Date: NPS was made mandatory for all new entrants joining Central Government service (except the Armed Forces) on or after 1st January 2004.
2. Adoption by GNCTD: The Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi (GNCTD) adopted the NPS framework for all employees appointed to Delhi Government departments and schools under the Directorate of Education joining on or after 1st January 2004.
3. Defined Contribution vs. Defined Benefit: NPS replaced the old defined-benefit pension scheme governed by the CCS (Pension) Rules, 1972. Under NPS, both the employee (10% of Basic Pay + DA) and the Government (revised to 14% of Basic Pay + DA) contribute monthly to the employee's Permanent Retirement Account (PRAN), which is professionally managed by PFRDA-registered Pension Funds.
4. Principal / DDO Role: The School Principal / DDO is responsible for timely PRAN generation, prompt deduction and uploading of monthly NPS contributions via the NSDL/CRA portal, ensuring zero delay in credit to employees' accounts.

1. प्रभावी कट-ऑफ तिथि: सशस्त्र बलों को छोड़कर, 1 जनवरी 2004 को या उसके बाद केंद्र सरकार की सेवा में शामिल होने वाले सभी नए कर्मचारियों के लिए एनपीएस को अनिवार्य बनाया गया।
2. दिल्ली सरकार द्वारा अंगीकरण: राष्ट्रीय राजधानी क्षेत्र दिल्ली सरकार (GNCTD) ने भी 1 जनवरी 2004 को या उसके बाद शिक्षा निदेशालय के स्कूलों तथा अन्य विभागों में नियुक्त होने वाले सभी शिक्षकों एवं कर्मचारियों के लिए एनपीएस लागू किया।
3. अंशदायी संरचना: एनपीएस ने सीसीएस (पेंशन) नियम, 1972 के तहत मिलने वाली पुरानी परिभाषित लाभ पेंशन योजना (OPS) का स्थान लिया। इसके तहत कर्मचारी का 10% (मूल वेतन + डीए) तथा सरकार का 14% अंशदान प्रतिमाह कर्मचारी के स्थायी सेवानिवृत्ति खाता संख्या (PRAN) में जमा किया जाता है, जिसका नियमन PFRDA द्वारा किया जाता है।
4. DDO/प्रधानाचार्य का कर्तव्य: स्कूल प्रमुख/DDO का यह दायित्व है कि वह नव-नियुक्त कर्मचारी का PRAN समय पर बनवाए और प्रतिमाह ट्रेजरी/N-CRA पोर्टल के माध्यम से अंशदान का सही क्रेडिट सुनिश्चित करे।

questions.explanation_english: Under Rule 28 of the CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972, government servants serving in a Vacation Department (such as teachers and academic staff in schools) are entitled to regular institutional summer, autumn, and winter vacations. Consequently, their regular Earned Leave (EL) entitlement is restricted compared to non-vacation staff (who receive 30 days of EL annually). Vacation staff receive an advance credit of 5 days on 1st January and 5 days on 1st July each calendar year, totaling 10 days of EL per annum. Furthermore, under Rule 28(1), if a teacher is formally retained on government duty during vacation by a specific written order of the competent authority and is prevented from availing of the vacation, additional EL is credited proportionately up to a maximum ceiling of 30 days per year.

Pursuing studies or appearing in examinations without prior written permission constitutes administrative misconduct inviting disciplinary action.

questions.explanation_english:
Under Rule 43-C of the Central Civil Services (Leave) Rules, 1972 and relevant DoPT notifications applicable to Delhi Government school employees:

1. Entitlement and Duration: A female government servant and single male government servant (unmarried, widower, or divorcee) may be granted Child Care Leave (CCL) for a maximum period of 730 days during their entire service for taking care of up to two eldest surviving children.
2. Age Limit: CCL can be availed for rearing or for looking after any needs of the children (like examination, sickness, etc.) until the children attain the age of eighteen (18) years.
3. Exception for Children with Benchmark Disabilities: The Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) removed the upper age limit of 18 years in the case of a child with benchmark disabilities (having a minimum disability of 40% certified by an authorized medical authority), allowing CCL irrespective of the child's age.
4. Leave Salary Provisions: 100% of leave salary is paid for the first 365 days, and 80% of leave salary is paid for the remaining 365 days. CCL cannot be availed for more than 3 spells in a calendar year.

2. आयु सीमा: यह अवकाश बच्चे के 18 वर्ष की आयु प्राप्त करने तक ही अनुमन्य है।
3. दिव्यांग बच्चों के मामले में छूट: यदि बच्चा दिव्यांग (Benchmark Disability 40% या अधिक) है, तो DoPT के संशोधित नियमों के तहत 18 वर्ष की आयु सीमा की शर्त हटा दी गई है, अर्थात दिव्यांग बच्चे हेतु किसी भी आयु तक CCL लिया जा सकता है।

questions.explanation_english: Under Fundamental Rule 9(21)(a)(i), 'Pay' is defined as the monthly amount drawn by a government servant which has been sanctioned for a post held by him substantively or in an officiating capacity, or to which he is entitled by reason of his position in a cadre, including basic pay, overseas pay, special pay, and personal pay, as well as any other emoluments specifically classed as pay by the President (such as Non-Practising Allowance / NPA). Allowances like Dearness Allowance (DA), House Rent Allowance (HRA), Transport Allowance (TA), and Children Education Allowance (CEA) are compensatory additions to pay designed to offset price escalation or specific expenses and are excluded from the fundamental definition of 'Pay'.
questions.explanation_hindi: मूल नियम (FR) 9(21)(a) के अनुसार 'वेतन' (Pay) का तात्पर्य उस मासिक धनराशि से है जो किसी सरकारी सेवक द्वारा धारित पद के लिए मूल वेतन (Basic Pay), व्यक्तिगत वेतन (Personal Pay), विशेष वेतन अथवा राष्ट्रपति द्वारा वेतन के रूप में वर्गीकृत अन्य परिलब्धियों (जैसे डॉक्टरों को दिया जाने वाला नॉन-प्रैक्टिसिंग अलाउंस / NPA) के रूप में प्राप्त की जाती है। महंगाई भत्ता (DA), मकान किराया भत्ता (HRA) तथा परिवहन भत्ता (TA) आदि प्रतिपूरक भत्तों (Compensatory Allowances) की श्रेणी में आते हैं, जो मुद्रास्फीति व जीवन-यापन के खर्चों की भरपाई हेतु दिए जाते हैं और वे 'वेतन' की मूल परिभाषा का हिस्सा नहीं होते हैं।
questions.topic: DoE Directorate of Education, Delhi: Circulars and Guidelines
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Dearness Allowance (DA)

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Fundamental Rule 9(21) defines pay as the monthly amount drawn by a government servant, including basic pay in the prescribed level, special pay, and personal pay. Allowances granted to compensate for specific living costs, such as Dearness Allowance or House Rent Allowance, are excluded from the core definition of pay.

questions.question_english: A student's parent formally requests to inspect the evaluated answer script of their ward for the annual final examination. Under the Right to Information Act, 2005 and departmental administrative guidelines, what is the procedurally correct course of action for the Head of School (HoS)?
options_english: Permit the student/parent to inspect the evaluated answer sheet and/or provide a certified copy upon request following the declaration of results
Summarily reject the application citing that evaluated examination answer sheets are privileged and strictly confidential institutional records
Decline inspection unless the applicant produces a formal mandatory writ or directive issued by a competent court of law
Hand over the physical original answer script permanently to the parent for home retention
questions.explanation_english: The procedural handling of evaluated answer sheets is governed by the landmark Supreme Court of India ruling in Central Board of Secondary Education & Anr. v. Aditya Bandopadhyay & Ors. (2011) 8 SCC 497. The Supreme Court unequivocally held that an evaluated answer script is 'information' held by the public examining authority/school under fiduciary relationship, and the examinee has the fundamental statutory right under the Right to Information (RTI) Act, 2005 to inspect their evaluated answer sheet and obtain certified copies thereof. The Directorate of Education, Delhi guidelines mandate that once the final results have been formally announced, schools must maintain transparency. The Head of School (as Public Information Officer or administrative head) must allow the student/parent to inspect the evaluated answer script or furnish photocopies upon application and payment of prescribed nominal fees. However, the original answer sheet remains the property of the school archives and cannot be permanently handed over, nor can the request be denied on grounds of confidentiality.
questions.explanation_hindi: मूल्यांकित उत्तर-पुस्तिकाओं के प्रकटीकरण से संबंधित विधिक स्थिति माननीय सर्वोच्च न्यायालय के ऐतिहासिक निर्णय सीबीएसई एवं अन्य बनाम आदित्य बंदोपाध्याय एवं अन्य (2011) द्वारा स्थापित की गई है। सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने स्पष्ट किया कि एक परीक्षार्थी सूचना का अधिकार (RTI) अधिनियम, 2005 की धारा 2(f) और 2(j) के तहत अपनी मूल्यांकित उत्तर-पुस्तिका का निरीक्षण करने तथा उसकी प्रमाणित छायाप्रति प्राप्त करने का पूर्ण विधिक अधिकार रखता है। शिक्षा निदेशालय, दिल्ली के दिशा-निर्देशों के अनुसार परीक्षा परिणाम घोषित होने के बाद विद्यालय प्रमुख (HoS) का यह विधिक एवं प्रशासनिक दायित्व है कि यदि छात्र अथवा उसके अभिभावक उत्तर-पुस्तिका के निरीक्षण की मांग करते हैं, तो उन्हें उत्तर-पुस्तिका का निरीक्षण कराया जाए अथवा नियमानुसार प्रमाणित प्रति उपलब्ध कराई जाए। मूल उत्तर-पुस्तिका विद्यालय का आधिकारिक अभिलेख होती है जिसे स्थायी रूप से सौंपा नहीं जा सकता, और न ही गोपनीयता की आड़ में निरीक्षण से मना किया जा सकता है।

questions.question_english:
Consider the following statutory and administrative records maintained in a recognized school under the Delhi School Education Rules, 1973:
I. Admission and Withdrawal Register (Scholar's Register)
II. Pupil's Daily Attendance Register
III. Monthly Acquittance Roll (Pay and Allowances)
Which of the above records are required to be preserved PERMANENTLY under the record retention schedule?
options_english: I only
I and II only
I and III only
I, II and III
questions.explanation_english:
Under Rule 142 and Schedule VI of the Delhi School Education Rules (DSEAR), 1973, read with the Record Retention Schedule of the Directorate of Education, Delhi: 
1. The 'Admission and Withdrawal Register' (commonly called the Scholar's Register) is a permanent legal document containing vital biographical details, date of birth, admission number, parents' particulars, and academic progression of every pupil admitted to the school. It must be preserved permanently in the school archives.
2. The 'Pupil's Daily Attendance Register' is an operational record preserved for a retention period of 3 to 5 years.
3. The 'Acquittance Roll' (records of payment of salaries and allowances) has a prescribed financial retention period (typically 35 years or until completion of all pensionary and audit requirements), but it is NOT classified as a permanent school record like the Admission Register. Therefore, only statement I is correct.
questions.explanation_hindi:
दिल्ली स्कूल शिक्षा नियमावली (DSEAR), 1973 के नियम 142 एवं अनुसूची VI तथा शिक्षा निदेशालय के अभिलेख प्रतिधारण कार्यक्रम (Record Retention Schedule) के अनुसार:
1. 'प्रवेश एवं निष्कासन रजिस्टर' (Admission and Withdrawal Register / Scholar's Register) एक स्थायी विधिक अभिलेख है जिसमें विद्यालय में प्रवेश लेने वाले प्रत्येक छात्र की जन्मतिथि, माता-पिता का नाम, प्रवेश संख्या तथा शैक्षिक प्रगति का आधिकारिक विवरण दर्ज होता है। इसे विद्यालय में आजीवन/स्थायी रूप से (Permanently) सुरक्षित रखा जाना अनिवार्य है।
2. 'छात्र दैनिक उपस्थिति रजिस्टर' एक कार्यवाहक अभिलेख है जिसे सामान्यतः 3 से 5 वर्ष तक सुरक्षित रखा जाता है।
3. 'वेतन भुगतान पावती रोल' (Acquittance Roll) एक वित्तीय दस्तावेज है जिसकी प्रतिधारण अवधि 35 वर्ष (या लेखापरीक्षा/पेंशन संबंधी औपचारिकताओं के पूर्ण होने तक) निर्धारित है, किंतु यह स्थायी (Permanent) श्रेणी में नहीं आता।
अतः केवल कथन I सही है।

key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) I only

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Statutory record preservation rules specify retention periods for various school documents. The Admission and Withdrawal Register contains permanent biographical and academic details of all admitted students, requiring permanent retention. Other operational records, such as daily pupil attendance registers and financial acquittance rolls, have defined non-permanent retention periods under record retention schedules.
